title: PIMnast: Balanced Data Placement for GEMV Acceleration with Processing-In-Memory
problem: While Processing-In-Memory (PIM) designs can boost memory bandwidth for GEMV operations, determining optimal data-placement strategies to distribute matrices across memory banks is a key impediment to achieving acceleration in GenAI inference.
motivation: GEMV operations dominate generative AI inference workloads and demand high memory bandwidth, making their acceleration critical for GenAI performance.
method: PIMnast identifies and balances multiple factors impacting data-placement for GEMV on PIM hardware that augments memory banks with compute capabilities and broadcasts commands across banks. The methodology applies orchestration knobs to optimize matrix distribution across banks and coordinates data placement with PIM's broadcast execution model.
key_novelty: A systematic methodology for determining optimal data-placement strategies that balance competing factors to maximize GEMV acceleration on PIM, achieving near-roofline performance.
contributions: Identification of key factors impacting data-placement for GEMV on PIM systems
PIMnast methodology for balanced data-placement achieving 6.86× speedup across GenAI models
Orchestration knobs and techniques for additional GEMV acceleration
Demonstration of 5× per-token latency speedup for GenAI inference workloads

metrics.speedup: 6.86× for GEMVs (86% of 7× roofline), 5× for per-token latencies

primary_theme: Optimizing data-placement strategies for PIM-accelerated GEMV in GenAI inference
